title: 第4章 限级面条
content_zh:
江城古往今来都是作为国之重镇的存在，历史文化沉淀极深，历朝历代的文物收藏品在这里都能寻到，淘宝者与收藏家络绎不绝来此，因此也形成了独特的古玩收藏文化。

古玩一条街就是江城藏品种类最齐全，各种藏友淘宝者最集中的地方，当然也能吸引那些来江城旅游的观光客，除了街道两旁古玩店铺林立之外，外围也形成了独特的地摊文化。几张报纸，一块旧布往地上一铺，摆上些老物件便可以做开了生意。

虽说同样是交着市场管理费，摆地摊也有位置差异，起早的占了个好位置一天总有几个生意上门，因此天还没大亮就有占位置的地摊主摆出了家当。

对于徐青而言仅仅是路过而已，对那些摆出的老物件啥的压根提不起半点兴趣，更何况他口袋里只有十块钱。

“这位小哥，帮老婆子买本书吧！”一个两鬓斑白的婆婆低声兜售起了地摊上的老旧书，没想到话刚出口就引来了旁边摊主们一阵哄笑。

“花婆子，你没看这小哥一脸的露水气儿，说不准是和家里闹别扭跑出来的，还有个毛心思看书……”一个穿铜钱装，戴瓜皮帽，打扮得像地主老财的摊主说道。

“瞧他那身行头，身上怕是连一张红的也掏不出来。”

徐青走得匆忙，穿着背心短裤，而且刚才在公园里摔了一跤，身上沾了不少草屑泥土啥的，看上去的确不像个有钱的主。

老婆婆无所谓的笑了笑手道：“这书最便宜的才五块钱一本，也不是什么贵东西，大清早的能开张也是个好兆头。”

“我看花婆子是想开张想昏头了，就您那几本语录和民国书也能值五块钱一本？”一旁又有人调侃。

花婆子每天清早就来占位，不过生意清淡无比，加上这两天没开张，才会主动吆喝，只希望能开张赚个好兆头。

鬼使神差的徐青居然停下了脚步，蹲在花婆子地摊旁随意翻看起那些旧书来，当他拿起一本掉了书皮的残破地图册时，右眼皮突的一跳，瞳孔中居然出现了一张薄薄的四方纸片，上面赫然印着一头大象，还写着大清，邮政局，五厘银等字样。

“邮票？”徐青心头一跳，连连翻看了几页，却发现这张印着大象的邮票竟和书页一起翻动，就好像粘在书页上一样。

尝试着用手指抠了抠书页，那张邮票居然动也不动，书页有夹层，一个念头瞬间闪过，徐青心头一惊，赶紧闭上了双眼，当他再次睁眼时，书页又恢复了原样，仿佛是刹那间的错觉一般。

“小哥，这书可是有些年头了，要是中意十块钱拿去，算是给老婆子开张了……”花婆子见徐青兴趣索然的模样，忍不住又开始小声咕叨起来。

“八块钱成么？我还能剩两块钱坐公交。”徐青放下地图册，拍了拍裤子上的草屑站起身来。

花婆子略一沉吟，拿起地图册一把塞到了徐青手中说道：“好，八块钱拿去……”

清早就能做成一单生意，冲这兆头就算徐青再压几块钱价花婆子也会接受，这本地图册她早就让人鉴定过，并非什么古籍孤本，很普通的早期印刷品，值不了几块钱。

徐青倒也爽快，从兜里掏出那张皱巴巴的钞票递了过去，随手把地图册卷了卷插进兜里，拿了零钱转身离开。

在外游荡了一夜，徐青已经做出了决定，回家，不管嫂子怎样埋怨他都要坚持把祝大姐介绍的活计做下去，再苦再累也要自食其力。

徐青并没有坐公交车，而是选择步行，省下来两块钱刚好能在楼下小吃档对付一个早餐。

走到早餐档又碰到熟人，美女房东祝晓玲，这时候她正低着头吸溜汤面，正好背对着徐青，不过从背影就能一眼认出来。

“老板，一碗两块的汤面……”徐青低声叫唤了一句，两块钱的汤粉在江城地头上已经很罕见了，只有这种偏僻的小吃档才有，也算是薄利多销吧。

这是一家父子档，老爹负责掌厨，二十出头的儿子就充当服务员的角色，这一声吆喝更是别出心裁，引得后来的两个年轻人也跟着凑起趣来。

“老板，给我一碗薄码肉丝面……”

“唔！我要有码的，多加点武藤兰……错了，是牛腩……”

一石激起千层浪，一个无码竟把武藤兰带了出来，引得食客们一阵爆笑。祝晓玲也诧异的回过头来，当她见到坐在身后的徐青时，眉头微微一皱，端着面碗直接走过来坐在了他对面。

正巧这时老板儿子把面端了过来，听到两人的对话微微一笑接口道：“吃面你用面条鲜啊！”说完指了指桌角的老抽。

祝晓玲想起了一句广告词儿，紧绷的嘴角顿时扬起一抹弯弧，瞧了一眼碗里的无码面，笑道：“帮他加点排骨。”

“好嘞！”那小子唱应的一声，又端着面碗走了回去。

“不用了……”徐青捏了捏口袋里两块钱，心里不免有些忐忑。

“什么不用，姐请你。”祝晓玲似乎看出了徐青的难处，微笑道：“昨晚跑去哪里了，害你嫂子一晚没睡，要是为难的话，昨天的事算我没说……”

“别，这活我一定要干，不过要麻烦你一件事儿。”徐青咬了咬嘴唇说道：“活我一定会做好，你别告诉我嫂子就行。”

“嗯！先回去好好休息，有活了打电话给你。”祝晓玲点头应了一声，起身结完帐走了。徐青望着她妙曼的背影，心里升起一丝被关怀的暖意。祝大姐人还是不错的，就是发脾气的模样彪悍了点。
content_en:
Jiangcheng has always been an important town in the country. It has a profound history and culture. Collections of cultural relics from past dynasties can be found here. Treasure hunters and collectors come here in an endless stream, so it has also formed a unique culture of antique collection.

Antique Street has the most comprehensive collections in Jiangcheng, and is where collectors of all kinds gather and hunt for treasures. Of course, it can also attract tourists who come to Jiangcheng. In addition to the numerous antique shops on both sides of the street, a unique street stall culture has also been formed on the periphery.Just spread a few newspapers, a piece of old cloth on the ground, and put some old items on it and you can start a business.

Although the market management fee is also paid, there are also differences in the location of the street stalls. Those who get up early and occupy a good position will always have several businesses coming to the door during the day. Therefore, before dawn, the stall owners who occupy the position will set out their belongings.

For Xu Qing, he was just passing by and had no interest in the old objects on display, not to mention he only had ten dollars in his pocket.

"Brother, help me buy a book for this old lady!" A mother-in-law with gray hair on her temples started selling old books on the stall in a low voice. Unexpectedly, the words just came out of her mouth, which caused a burst of laughter from the stall owners nearby.

"Mrs. Hua, didn't you see the dewy look on this guy's face? He might have run out because of a disagreement with his family, and he's still reading a book..." said a stall owner who was wearing a copper coin suit and a melon skin hat, dressed like a rich landlord.

"Look at his outfit, I'm afraid he can't even take out a red card."

Xu Qing was walking in a hurry, wearing a tank top and shorts. He had fallen down in the park just now and had a lot of grass clippings and dirt on his body. He really didn't look like a rich man.

The old woman smiled nonchalantly and said, "The cheapest book is only five yuan a copy. It's not expensive. It's a good sign that it's open early in the morning."

"I think Hua Pozi is going crazy trying to open a business. Are your quotations and books on the Republic of China worth five yuan each?" Someone else ridiculed.

Mrs. Hua comes to take a seat early every morning, but the business is very light, and it has not been open for the past two days, so she takes the initiative to shout, hoping to open and make a good omen.

Xu Qing unexpectedly stopped and squatted beside Hua Pozi's stall, casually browsing through the old books. When he picked up a broken atlas with the cover off, his right eyelid suddenly jumped, and a thin square piece of paper appeared in his pupil. An elephant was printed on it, and the words Qing Dynasty, Post Office, and Five Cents of Silver were written on it.

"Stamps?" Xu Qing's heart skipped a beat, and he flipped through several pages, only to find that the stamp with the elephant on it was flipping with the page, as if it was stuck to the page.

He tried to pick at the page with his fingers, but the stamp did not move. There were gaps in the page. An idea flashed across his mind. Xu Qing was startled and quickly closed his eyes. When he opened his eyes again, the page returned to its original state, as if it was an illusion in an instant.

"Brother, this book is quite old. If you like it and get it for ten yuan, it will be considered as a book for the old lady..." Seeing Xu Qing's lack of interest, Mrs. Hua couldn't help but start mumbling in a low voice again.

"Is eight yuan enough? I still have two yuan left to take the bus." Xu Qing put down the atlas, patted the grass clippings on his pants and stood up.

Mrs. Hua pondered for a moment, then picked up the atlas and stuffed it into Xu Qing's hand and said, "Okay, take the eight yuan..."

A deal can be made early in the morning. This is a sign that even if Xu Qing presses a few more yuan, the old woman will accept it. She has already had this atlas appraised. It is not an isolated ancient book. It is a very ordinary early printing and is not worth a few yuan.

Xu Qing was happy. He took out the crumpled banknote from his pocket and handed it over. He rolled up the atlas and put it in his pocket, took the change and turned around to leave.

After wandering out all night, Xu Qing has made a decision to go home. No matter how much his sister-in-law complains, he will insist on doing the work introduced by Sister Zhu. No matter how hard and tired he is, he must support himself.

Xu Qing chose to walk instead of taking the bus. The two yuan he saved was just enough for breakfast at the snack stall downstairs.

When I walked to the breakfast stall, I ran into an acquaintance again, the beautiful landlady Zhu Xiaoling. At this time, she was lowering her head to sip the soup noodles. Her back was turned to Xu Qing, but she could be recognized at a glance from her back.

"Boss, a bowl of noodle soup costs two yuan..." Xu Qing called in a low voice. Noodle soup that costs two yuan is very rare in Jiangcheng. It can only be found in such remote snack stalls. It can be considered a small profit but quick turnover.

This is a father-son stall, with the father in charge of cooking and the son in his early twenties acting as the waiter. This shout was even more original and attracted the two young people who followed him to join in the fun.

"Boss, give me a bowl of thinly sliced pork noodles..."

"Hmm! I want it to be more precise and add more Wutenglan...wrong, it's beef brisket..."

One stone stirred up a thousand waves, and an uncoded man actually brought out Wu Tenglan, which caused a burst of laughter from the diners.Zhu Xiaoling also turned around in surprise. When she saw Xu Qing sitting behind her, she frowned slightly, walked over with a noodle bowl and sat opposite him.

It happened that the boss's son brought the noodles over. Hearing the conversation between the two, he smiled slightly and said: "You should use fresh noodles to eat noodles!" After saying this, he pointed to the old soy sauce on the corner of the table.

Zhu Xiaoling remembered an advertisement slogan, and the corners of her tight mouth suddenly raised an arc. She glanced at the uncensored noodles in the bowl and said with a smile: "Add some ribs for him."

"Okay!" The boy responded and walked back with the noodle bowl.

"No need..." Xu Qing squeezed the two dollars in his pocket, feeling a little uneasy.

"No need, sister, please." Zhu Xiaoling seemed to see Xu Qing's difficulty and smiled: "Where did you go last night? Your sister-in-law didn't sleep all night. If you are in trouble, I didn't say what happened yesterday..."

"No, I have to do this job, but I have to trouble you with something." Xu Qing bit her lip and said, "I will definitely do the job well, just don't tell my sister-in-law."

"Well! Go back and have a good rest. I'll call you when I'm alive." Zhu Xiaoling nodded in agreement, got up, paid the bill and left.Xu Qing looked at her graceful back, and felt a warm feeling of care in his heart.Sister Zhu is still a nice person, but she looks a bit tough when she loses her temper.
